children: The Federal Reserve is mapping out a proposal to increase the thresholds that require stricter oversight of big banks, according to a media report on Friday.

The bank regulator is expected to soon propose recalibrating the thresholds — at which banks are required to conduct stress tests and follow other strict rules — to account for inflation and economic growth, Reuters reported, citing four people with knowledge of the matter. Three of the people said they expect the proposal to be made later this year.

Regulators progressively increase requirements as banks' assets grow, with current rules imposing stricter requirements at $100B, $250B, and $700B. Lenders complain that those thresholds, which were set in 2019, don't account for economic growth. That subjects banks to oversight that's stricter than warranted for the risk they pose, they contend.
The central bank, which regulates the country's largest banks, plans to boost the highest threshold closer to $1T and the lower threshold closer to $150B, Reuters reported.
